newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea sees USDA rallies being met by selling.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea sees USDA rallies being met by selling.

text.p: South Korean grain and oilseed buyers said on Monday they were not concerned that U.S. futures prices might be pushed into a sharp uptrend by Friday's bullish USDA crop figures as they expect rallies to meet solid selling.
Most local corn buyers are unlikely to move into the market this week as they believe U.S. farmers will take advantage of the surge in Chicago futures to lock in sales, they said.

"Buyers will hold back their purchases since they expect U.S. farmers' selling to come out soon," a trader with a Seoul-based grain trading house said, adding that purchasers would wait for the markets to calm down.

But some South Korean feed makers are expected to be forced to begin buying feed grain to cover their needs for nearby shipment as they are unable to delay their purchases any longer, a trader with National Livestock Coopertives Federation said.
"We expect several buyers to start covering their grain purchases for nearby shipment since they can not delay any more," the NLCF trader said.
"We had a meeting early Monday morning to analyse last Friday's price surge and discuss our further buying plans," an official with a local soybean processor said.

"It will affect us if the bullish trend goes on longer, but we don't expect much impact right now from the USDA report since we are normally buying soybeans on a basis price (at a premium to Chicago futures)," the official said.

He said his company would buy 15,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans this week for shipment in early February. An official with another soybean processor said his company would buy 50,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans by mid-January for shipment in February.
He said the bulk grains freight rate to South Korea from the U.S. Pacific Northwest remained unchanged from last week at between $14 to $14.50 a tonne and from the U.S. Gulf at between $24 to $24.50.
